overview: The file consists of eleven State Department jacket-index sheets summarizing correspondence, reports, clippings, translations, and cross-references concerning narcotics regulation and illicit drug traffic in the Kwantung Leased Territory, especially Dairen, from about 1930 through 1939, with references to earlier cases. Its entries document opium monopolies and addiction statistics, clandestine morphine factories, cocaine and “benzolin” smuggling, prosecutions and sentences, suspected international traffickers, and the movement of suspects among Dairen, Shanghai, Tientsin, Harbin, and other ports. The sheets also reveal sustained information-sharing among American consular posts, the State and Treasury Departments, the Bureau of Narcotics, foreign authorities, and the League of Nations.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: early narcotics correspondence concerning Dairen
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: An index sheet records early 1930 correspondence about illicit narcotics distribution and regulatory control in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The entries concern missing or incomplete consular despatches, press reports in the Manchuria Daily News, the identification of a drug reported as “benzoin,” and allegations that Dairen was a distribution center for opium and other dangerous drugs. They also record instructions about the number and distribution of despatch copies and reference an $800,000 opium seizure at Mukden.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: prosecutions, benzolin, and the opium monopoly
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: A continuation index summarizes late-1930 and 1931 records on narcotics prosecutions, drug terminology, seizures, and the Kwantung opium monopoly.
subfiles.summary: The sheet links Dairen’s illicit trade with Hamburg and Japan and describes indictments for post-1927 trafficking supported by falsified documents. It lists defendants in the Dairen “benzolin” prosecution, notes a Japan Chronicle clipping on the government opium monopoly, and records a morphine seizure and related Osaka prosecutions.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: George I. Tribe and associated narcotics suspects, copy one
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: An index sheet catalogs correspondence on the arrest and investigation of George I. Tribe and other suspects in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: The entries follow Tribe’s arrest by Japanese authorities, State Department requests for reports, and concern about possible United States connections. They identify Japanese and foreign associates, including Kokichi Koike, Shigeru Sumida, Nathan Granovsky, Boris Bogdanovsky, and Jacob D. Lelchitzky, and also reference alleged transactions involving Henri Bacri Cohen and R. Takashima.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: George I. Tribe and associated narcotics suspects, duplicate sheet
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: A second version of the jacket sheet repeats and slightly revises entries on Tribe, his alleged associates, and the Bacri–Takashima case.
subfiles.summary: This duplicate supplies variant spellings for several suspects and again records requests for reports, the New York Times clipping on six arrests, and information obtained from the Kwantung Government. It also notes the opening of Tribe’s trial and his claim that the three transactions were local and lacked a broader overseas connection.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Tribe investigation and secret morphine factory
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes 1932 correspondence on George I. Tribe, a clandestine Japanese morphine factory, and the Gourevich case.
subfiles.summary: Treasury supplied a San Francisco narcotics-agent’s report on Tribe and circulated a British report naming fourteen men allegedly involved in a secret morphine factory near Dairen. The Department ordered Dairen to report on the factory and requested the outcome of the Bacri–Takashima and Gourevich cases. A later entry assesses the significance of a four-kilogram cocaine import and records Fujita Shokai’s inquiry into British cocaine prices.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Fujita Shokai, Gourevich, and Dairen drug factories
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: An index sheet records late-1932 and early-1933 reports on cocaine purchasing, Gourevich, clandestine factories, and proposed Korean opium production.
subfiles.summary: Entries include a League document on Fujita Shokai’s inquiry into British cocaine prices and instructions to keep the Department and the Treasury Attaché in Shanghai informed about Gourevich. The sheet records Jacob Gourevich’s sentence and lists suspects in a clandestine morphine factory near Dairen. It also notes a proposal to increase opium cultivation in Korea to replace Persian supplies to Kwantung.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: 1932 Dairen cases, laws, budgets, and suspect movements
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: This sheet indexes reports on Fujita Shokai, Dairen narcotics cases, governing regulations, opium revenue, and the movements of suspects.
subfiles.summary: The entries describe Fujita Shokai’s activities in Dairen and Changchun and name several people implicated in 1932 narcotics cases. They reference a substantial summary of narcotics laws and regulations and a report on the Kwantung government budget and opium-monopoly revenue. Later entries track suspects traveling to Tientsin and report Boris Bogdanovsky’s arrest, seized notebook, and release after returning from Shanghai.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: benzolin case and international suspect files
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: An index sheet covers reports on suspect movements, South Manchuria Railway opium regulations, the benzolin case, and Boris Bogdanovsky’s contacts.
subfiles.summary: The sheet transmits reports about Devineau, Shifman, Gourevitch, and persons involved in the Bacri–Takashima case, as well as regulations governing opium in the South Manchuria Railway areas. It records convictions and a retrial involving T. Shirakawa and nine others for illegal benzolin imports. Additional entries concern George Israel Tribe’s new passport and names found in Boris Bogdanovsky’s notebook, including contacts connected with Los Angeles and United States visa efforts.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: morphine plants, foreign suspects, and maritime traffic
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes reports on Dairen morphine plants, suspect movements, Greek steamships, and narcotics manufacture and distribution.
subfiles.summary: Several entries detail the discovery of morphine plants, identify implicated persons, and report sentences. Curt Smith and the Kapustins were monitored in Dairen, while Treasury communications summarized narcotic factories through reports from Shanghai. The sheet also lists Greek steamships and suspected traffickers who visited Dairen in early 1935 and references further reports on drug manufacture and factory discoveries.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: regional narcotics reports and international intelligence
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: This index sheet records 1935–1937 reports on regional opium markets, smuggling, Chinese legislation, Dairen intelligence, and international suspects.
subfiles.summary: Treasury reports surveyed opium shops and secret factories in Harbin, Antung, Dairen, Changchun, and another locality rendered as Tennyi, while consular officers discussed smuggling at Yokohama and the effects of Chinese legislation. Other entries concern narcotics control in Kwantung, the morphine-poisoning death of Harold S. Jones, and Max Kattwinkel’s statement about Curt Smith to German authorities. The sheet also records Commander Thompson’s report after visiting Dairen and a later China report on A. Beerbrayer.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Kwantung opium monopoly and addiction statistics
subfiles.doc_type: list of papers / jacket index sheet
subfiles.about: The final index sheet catalogs 1938–1939 reports, ordinances, and statistics concerning the Kwantung Leased Territory opium monopoly.
subfiles.summary: Turner’s reports describe the monopoly, transmit translations of Japanese imperial and Kwantung Bureau ordinances, and include a sample empty opium tube. One entry gives a total of 28,197 permitted opium smokers, while another reports an increase among Japanese addicts. The final entry cites 1937 trade statistics published by the Kwantung Bureau at Hsinking, now Changchun.

interest: These sheets are valuable as a compact finding aid to a decade of records that may otherwise be dispersed among State, Treasury, Bureau of Narcotics, personal-name, and League of Nations files. They expose the administrative machinery behind narcotics surveillance as well as a transnational network of suspects, shipping connections, factories, courts, and police authorities centered on Dairen. Especially useful are the many personal names, cross-references, ordinance citations, prosecution outcomes, and quantitative details such as the 28,197 licensed opium smokers; the duplicate sheet also preserves revealing spelling variants that can assist archival name searches.
